detail.abstract: We develop a theory of endogenous faction formation, in which faction success depends on coordinated collective action and members' unobservable intrinsic loyalty to overcome politically-vital coordination difficulties. detail.abstract: In the distributed assembly permutation flowshop, jobs are processed in identical flowshop factories and then assembled into products on one machine; the makespan is minimised. Heuristics are usually compared on a benchmark from 2013, whose large instances have no peer-reviewed lower bound. We computed lower bounds for all instances, including a decomposition bound that solves one small factory problem per product. On 751 of the 810 large instances (93%) the bound equals the makespan of a released schedule, which is therefore optimal, and an exact model proves 17 more optimal, 768 (95%) in all. The benchmark is easy, and the bounds explain why: the generator tends to make the assembly machine the bottleneck, and whether the closed-form bound is then reached depends mainly on whether the first product assembled has more jobs than there are factories. Our re-implementations of three published search methods and our own search differ there by at most 0.016 percentage points, whereas on a hard set of the same sizes, obtained by rescaling only the assembly times, the spread between the best and the worst is several hundred times larger, and the benchmark's best in our runs loses to two others on nearly every hard instance.

title: Union-of-Predecessors Bounds and a Forward-Backward Local Search for Multi-door Cross-dock Truck Scheduling

detail.title: Union-of-Predecessors Bounds and a Forward-Backward Local Search for Multi-door Cross-dock Truck Scheduling

detail.abstract: At a cross-docking terminal, an outbound truck can start loading only after every inbound truck that carries its goods, i.e., its predecessors, has been unloaded. In this article, we schedule the trucks on several doors per side to make the makespan as small as possible. On the public benchmark, published schedules lie 26% to 30% above the best known lower bounds. We wanted to know whether this optimality gap was the fault of the schedules or of the bounds, and we found that it is mostly the fault of the bounds. The earlier bounds reason about one truck at a time. Our bound asks instead which outbound trucks can have started by a given time. Their predecessors must have been unloaded by then, and thus this is a knapsack problem, and its solution gives a bound that we prove valid. On the benchmark our bound is on average 15.8% above the best earlier bound, and with it the mean gap of the published schedules of HgR, a hybrid Lagrangian metaheuristic, falls from 26.1% to 9.1%. Where optima are known, almost all of the remaining gap lies in the bound, which a second, stronger bound narrows further. When we add the knapsack argument as cuts to an exact constraint solver, it proves optimality on 137 of 300 newly generated instances, against 47 without them. Our local search, which also rebuilds schedules backwards in time, beats a published evolutionary algorithm at equal effort. On a structured set of new instances, with sparse or block predecessor sets, unbalanced door numbers and up to 300 inbound trucks, the bound gains much less.

detail.abstract: This study critically examines the role of managers in utilizing social networking platforms to develop effective customer service strategies, with a focused case analysis of Checkmate INC Pakistan, a Marketing Communications organization operating in a rapidly evolving digital environment. The research explores how managers adopt and implement social media tools to enhance customer engagement, formulate marketing strategies, and leverage the broader benefits of social networking to support organizational goals. Using a mixed-method approach, data were collected through structured questionnaires from 50 employees and in-depth interviews with five department managers. Quantitative findings reveal strong and significant relationships between managerial use of social networking and key organizational factors, including customer service performance, marketing strategy development, and recognition of social media benefits. The results highlight that managers who actively engage with social platforms are better positioned to understand customer needs, respond promptly to concerns, and design data-driven strategies that strengthen customer relationships. Qualitative insights support these findings, underscoring the growing importance of digital competencies among managerial staff. The study concludes with practical recommendations for Checkmate INC Pakistan to enhance managerial autonomy, training, and strategic integration of social media, ultimately contributing to improved customer service outcomes and competitive advantage in the Marketing Communications sector.

detail.abstract: Global health reform debates, including the 2026 Accra Reset, endorse "one plan, one budget, one report" but say little about how money should flow once it is mobilised. Sector-wide approaches and national health compacts have not resolved this. We propose that a costed, prioritised health benefits package serve as the organising unit of global health finance, with domestic and external funders co-financing the same package rather than separate programmes. Using Sierra Leone as a case study, where 88% of external health funding was off-budget in 2020-2024 and out-of-pocket payments were 54% of health spending in 2023 despite a free health care policy, we set out five elements to operationalise this shift: (1) a joint Ministry of Health and Ministry of Finance commitment to finance a prioritised package; (2) a single published co-financing schedule in dollars per person per year; (3) pooled procurement retained for price, with performance judged by availability at the point of care; (4) transparent governance with published criteria, public consultation and annual publication; and (5) a shared scorecard tracking effective coverage, equity and budget execution, with pre-agreed responses when commitments slip. We show how Sierra Leone's provisional package (about US$8 per person for the foundational tier; US$19 for Tier 1) could be jointly financed by the government, the Global Fund, Gavi and others, and set out what governments, funder boards and development banks would need to change. We offer the framework as an operational hypothesis to test in early-mover countries.

detail.abstract: ehubX is an open-source Python framework for the optimization-based planning of multi-energy systems, from buildings and districts to regions and countries. Users describe demands, candidate technologies such as heat pumps, photovoltaics, wind turbines, batteries and aquifer thermal energy storage, networks, and energy imports with prices and emissions in YAML and CSV files. ehubX then determines which technologies to install, when, at what capacity, and how to operate them to minimize cost or net CO 2 emissions, to maximize self-sufficiency, or to trade off two of these objectives. By default, it formulates a mixed-integer linear program that is solved by an external solver. Energy carriers and materials such as CO 2 are balanced as commodities, so that carbon capture, utilization and storage is planned together with the energy supply. Networks of interconnected sites, multi-stage pathways and time-series aggregation that retains seasonal storage are supported.

detail.abstract: The European Union's Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) and its Digital Product Passport (DPP) establish what textile producers must eventually disclose about a product's durability, recyclability, and substances of concern. They say little about where inside a supplier's own workflow those properties are actually decided. This paper argues that physical recyclability in commercial textiles is largely fixed at the design desk, in fibre blend selection, surface repeat and print coverage setting, colour and chemistry specification, and functional finish choice, well before a strike-off is approved and long before a life cycle assessment (LCA) or passport entry is compiled. Export mills, however, typically lack a structured governance mechanism for evaluating these decisions at the moment they are made. We propose a five-gate stage-gate decision framework, adapting Cooper's Stage-Gate systems theory to Design for Recycling (DfR), that places explicit go, hold, and redesign decisions at fibre selection, surface repeat and binder calculation, prepress calibration, recovery pre-audit, and tech-pack release. We outline a qualitative, practitioner-centred study design in which the framework is developed, stress-tested, and refined through semi-structured interviews with 8 to 12 designers, prepress and colour engineers, merchandisers, and compliance or sustainability managers in export-oriented textile production. The aim is to locate where recyclability-relevant decisions are currently made, by whom, and on what evidence, and to specify gate criteria that could reduce non-recyclable yardage and physical sampling runs. We position this as a study-design and framework preprint intended to seed a larger empirical programme, not as a completed empirical investigation.

detail.abstract: Time-series foundation models such as Kronos, TimesFM and Chronos can produce a plausible future price path from a short history. They do not tell the user how far to trust that path, whether their intervals hold up out of sample, or what the path means for the risk numbers that a risk desk reads. This paper describes Tycheon, an Apache-2.0 open-source library that adds that missing layer. Tycheon enforces point-in-time data access with two clocks per observation, wraps any forecaster in conformal calibration whose status is earned on a holdout, translates calibrated sample paths into Value at Risk, Expected Shortfall, drawdown probabilities and stress scenarios, and scores every model with a leakage-guarded walk-forward engine against a mandatory random-walk baseline and a Diebold-Mariano test. We report two results and are explicit about their limits. First, on a small synthetic benchmark (3 series, 108 pooled forecast origins), no model, including zero-shot Kronos-mini, was statistically distinguishable from the random walk, and Kronos-mini's nominal 90% interval contained 57.4% of outcomes. Second, a single manual check on real daily equity data showed that two-sided conformal calibration fitted on 60 recent origins reduced a 5-day 95% VaR from 5.38% to 3.93%, about 27%, making the position look safer than it was. We describe the resulting design rule, that calibration may only widen the tails used for risk figures, and its consequences. Multi-asset portfolio risk is always labelled uncalibrated, because the dependence between assets is assumed. Neither result is evidence about forecasting skill in real markets. The contribution is infrastructure: a forecast contract, a calibration and risk pipeline, and an evaluation protocol that publishes results whichever way they fall.

detail.abstract: Webrooming, the practice of searching for products online before purchasing in a physical store, is widespread yet we do not know whether it causally increases in-store spending or merely reflects consumers' underlying purchase intentions. We study the causal effect of webrooming using a randomized field experiment with a leading do-it-yourself (DIY) retailer in Chile. The experiment exposed 1.3 million online shoppers to alternative product recommendation policies, with more than 97,000 identifiable customers tracked across channels. Using randomized recommendation assignment as an instrument for online browsing, we estimate that each additional product browsed inflates in-store spending in that category by about 200 times compared to the baseline. The effect peaks in the following week and becomes statistically insignificant by the third week. We find no statistically significant reduction in concurrent online sales. Heterogeneity analyses suggest stronger responses among professional customers, new online customers, and categories with lower online purchase shares. These findings establish that online product exploration is a valuable driver of subsequent offline revenue and contradict the conventional emphasis on minimizing the path to online checkout. Put differently, for functional products such as DIY, stimulating unplanned product discovery clicks can be profitable, not because of additional online sales, but rather increased offline purchases.

detail.abstract: In classical information theory and algorithmic complexity applied to finite sequences, lower bounds for coding, statistical divergence, and structural complexity are almost universally defined by assuming that the input set Σ N is passively evaluated in its canonical identity representation (f = id). Although foundational studies in the non-asymptotic regime, such as those by Kontoyiannis and Verdú (2014) and by Painsky, Rosset, and Feder (2016), introduced optimization with respect to internal bijections f : Σ N → Σ N , such approaches remain invariant and yield no gain when evaluated on average over the uniform distribution of all possible inputs. In this paper, we prove that any theoretical bound associated with an empirical or structural cost function F (s) that does not account for dimension-expanding bijective transformations f : Σ N → Y ⊂ Σ N ′ (with N ′ > N and |Y | = |Σ N |), formalized by Set Shaping Theory (SST), constitutes a local representation-bound limit rather than a fundamental limit of information. We axiomatically formulate the Representation-Optimal Limit (L * F) and extend Set Shaping Theory beyond zero-order empirical entropy N H 0 (s), applying it to the Krichevsky-Trofimov universal redundancy L KT (s), k-th order conditional empirical entropy (N H k (s)), Kullback-Leibler divergence N D KL (P s ∥ Q) (Cachin's steganographic limit), and Gap Entropy on succinct data structures and graphs. Finally, we present the results of exact numerical evaluations and computational simulations that quantify the systematic reduction of both the average value and the worst-case value across all possible inputs.This article participates to Set Shaping Theory simulator project available at https: //sst-simulator.github.io/Set-Shaping-Theory-Simulator/.

detail.abstract: Refugee case records maintained by social workers contain rich narrative information about the circumstances, vulnerabilities, and needs of forcibly displaced individuals and families. However, the unstructured nature of these records limits their systematic use for early risk detection and service planning. This study explores the application of Natural Language Processing (NLP) to analyze refugee case records documented by social workers, with the aim of identifying linguistic signals associated with "destitution risk"-the likelihood that a refugee client will fall into or remain in extreme material deprivation, including homelessness, lack of income, and inability to meet basic needs. Using a corpus of anonymized case notes, we apply a combination of text preprocessing, feature extraction, and supervised classification techniques to detect indicators of destitution risk, complemented by topic modeling and keyword-in-context analysis to characterize the language social workers use when describing precarity. We further examine how identified risk signals map onto documented intervention pathways, including emergency housing referrals, financial assistance, legal support, and employment integration services. Preliminary findings suggest that specific lexical and semantic patterns-such as references to housing instability, informal employment, debt, and withdrawal of support-are associated with elevated destitution risk and with particular intervention trajectories. The study contributes a methodological framework for transforming qualitative case documentation into actionable risk intelligence, while attending to ethical considerations surrounding privacy, bias, and the responsible use of algorithmic tools in social service contexts. Implications for early warning systems, caseload prioritization, and evidencebased intervention design in refugee support services are discussed.

detail.abstract: Across public administration, recruitment, employment, and exchange, defensive and calculative behavior can emerge in relationships often analyzed through separate institutional literatures. Existing scholarship illuminates proceduralization, administrative burden, auditability, attention constraints, and strategic response, but the sequence linking relational redesign to differentiated adaptation remains less explicitly integrated across domains. This conceptual paper proposes that actors with disproportionate control over interaction formats can recast relationships as standardized, transactional, or risk-managed encounters, transferring coordination costs, proof obligations, waiting uncertainty, and responsibility downward. Where a gate is difficult to replace and further engagement retains expected value, intensified contact becomes more attractive; where alternative gates are available and additional attempts are inexpensive, diversification becomes more attractive. Proof requirements favor documentation, temporal pressure with weak outside options favors concession, and weakened reciprocal expectations favor shorter commitments. Feedback differs across branches: same-gate escalation may redirect attention or add review work, while widespread cross-gate diversification can enlarge recipient pools. Where these pressures induce further filtering or reduce informative feedback, uncertainty can reinforce defensive adaptation. The paper illustrates the branching mechanism through public complaint systems, recruitment and submission markets, workplace commitment, and a brief agricultural bargaining vignette. Rather than treating calculation as evidence of moral decline, it examines how institutional arrangements alter the relative payoffs of available actions without denying individual agency or responsibility. Its contribution is a conditional cross-domain causal framework for future comparative testing, not a universal account or empirically validated predictive model.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth of urban mobility data has enabled personalized transportation recommendation systems that suggest routes, modes, and departure times tailored to individual travelers. However, these systems typically rely on centralized data collection, raising serious privacy concerns and creating regulatory compliance challenges, particularly when recommendations must generalize across multiple cities with heterogeneous mobility patterns and non-shared data silos. This paper proposes a federated learning framework for privacypreserving transportation recommendation that enables multiple cities to collaboratively train a shared recommendation model without exchanging raw user trajectory, trip, or preference data. Our approach incorporates (i) a cross-city federated optimization strategy that handles non-IID mobility distributions and uneven data volumes across participating cities, (ii) a personalized federization mechanism that adapts the global model to local travel contexts while preserving knowledge transfer across cities, and (iii) privacy-preserving aggregation with differential privacy guarantees to protect against inference attacks on model updates. We evaluate the framework on real-world multi-city transportation datasets, comparing it against centralized training and local-only baselines in terms of recommendation accuracy, cold-start performance for data-scarce cities, and privacy leakage risk. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves recommendation quality comparable to centralized approaches while significantly reducing privacy exposure, and that cross-city collaboration particularly benefits cities with limited mobility data. The findings suggest that federated learning offers a viable pathway for building accurate, scalable, and privacy-respecting transportation recommendation services in multi-city deployments.

detail.abstract: COID-19 has resulted in increased e-commerce activity, which has highlighted the need for businesses to invest in good experiences because in a competitive online environment it is easy to compare products and prices among competitors. This has led to increased interest in optimising shopping cart performance within businesses. Simultaneously, academic research became interested in the factors that impact online shopping cart abandonment (OSCA). Academic research in this area has uncovered numerous variables that impact consumers' online behaviour. It is argued that these variables however are merely proximity explanations of something deeper and thus do not explain the why behind online consumer decision-making. Therefore, this study proposes that prospect theory is used to understand how consumers calculate perceived benefits and losses compared to a psychological goal in the mind of the consumer. Furthermore, it is suggested that evolutionary psychology with the fundamental-motives framework provides new insights into the ultimate consumer motivations that drive online behaviour. Then the applicability of five motivations and their applicability to website development and optimisation are discussed.

detail.abstract: A recent confluence of events has made AI regulation one of the most critical policy debates of our time. Proponents of increased AI regulation point to significant risks, including environmental harms, autonomous hacking, algorithmic bias, and catastrophic existential threats, arguing that current legal frameworks are inadequate. However, a counterargument involving the geopolitical cost of increased regulation must also be weighed in this debate. Increasing the regulatory burdens on AI development in the United States could stifle domestic innovation, allowing adversarial nations to dominate AI development. If authoritarian regimes dictate the future of AI, the resulting framework will reflect values of surveillance and censorship rather than liberal democracy and free expression. This Essay strengthens this argument by analogizing to the development of the internet, where a business-friendly environment and liability shields like Section 230 allowed U.S. firms to thrive and export these principles, thus embedding free speech norms into the internet framework. Likewise, maintaining U.S. dominance in AI development not only benefits the U.S. economy, but also serves as a vital safeguard for global democratic principles against digital authoritarianism. By understanding this geopolitical reality, policymakers can more accurately weigh the tradeoffs involved in AI regulation.

detail.abstract: Research and publication ethics are essential for ensuring the integrity, credibility, and responsible communication of scholarly knowledge. This chapter examines the philosophical foundations of ethics and their application to scientific research, with particular attention to research integrity, fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, redundant publication, salami slicing, selective reporting, data misrepresentation, authorship, and conflicts of interest. It discusses publication ethics, relevant guidelines, publication misconduct, complaints and appeals, and the identification of predatory journals. The chapter also introduces open-access publishing, self-archiving policies, journal-selection resources, plagiarism-detection software, and reference management tools, including Zotero and Mendeley. Furthermore, it explains the role of indexing and citation databases, such as Web of Science and Scopus, and introduces major journal-level and author-level indicators, including the Journal Impact Factor, CiteScore, SCImago Journal Rank (SJR), Source Normalized Impact per Paper (SNIP), Impact per Publication (IPP), h-index, g-index, and i10-index, alongside altmetrics. By integrating ethical principles with practical tools for scholarly communication and research evaluation, the chapter aims to develop researchers' ability to make informed 1 publication decisions, acknowledge intellectual contributions, evaluate scholarly sources critically, and interpret research indicators responsibly. It emphasizes that research metrics complement, but cannot replace, qualitative assessment of research quality and ethical scholarly judgement.

detail.abstract: The Basel III Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB) establishes the 97.5% Expected Shortfall (ES) as the primary measure for market-risk capital. Yet, because ES is not elicitable on its own (Gneiting, 2011; Fissler and Ziegel, 2016), regulatory backtesting primarily evaluates the accompanying Value-at-Risk (VaR), leaving the capital measure itself insufficiently validated. This paper examines whether commonly used ES models adequately capture tail-loss severity, particularly during periods of financial stress. Using daily data from 2000–2026 across six assets representing equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, and cryptocurrency, we evaluate four ES forecasting approaches: historical simulation, Gaussian, GARCH-t, and gradient-boosted quantile ES. Our validation framework combines the Acerbi–Székely and McNeil–Frey backtests with a regime-conditional ES severity ratio (ΛES) and a formal test of regime-dependent model performance. The results reveal systematic stress-regime underestimation of realized tail losses, ranging from approximately 10% to 44%, while calm-regime severity remains broadly consistent with predicted ES. The regime effect is statistically significant in 83% of model–asset combinations at the FRTB-relevant 97.5% confidence level. Importantly, unconditional ES backtests can indicate adequate model performance even when regime-conditional diagnostics identify significant deficiencies, exposing a critical limitation of conventional validation approaches. To address this problem, we introduce a transparent, regime-aware split-conformal recalibration procedure that brings stress-regime severity ratios close to unity and improves ES backtesting performance. These findings demonstrate that unconditional backtesting alone may provide false reassurance regarding the adequacy of market-risk capital estimates. We propose regime-conditional severity testing as an auditable complement to existing FRTB validation practices, strengthening model-risk governance under changing market conditions. This study extends Neupane (2026a) from regime-dependent VaR breach frequency to the severity of the Expected Shortfall capital measure.

detail.abstract: Two published studies report that air pollution moves the price gap between the Shanghai (A) and Hong Kong (H) listings of the same Chinese firm, and attribute it to different behavioural channels. Because the two listings carry identical cash-flow rights but trade to investor populations of which only one breathes Shanghai air, the sign of the response separates mood (negative), cognitive impairment (positive) and a response common to both populations (zero). Instrumenting daily Shanghai PM2.5 with dispersion conditions (effective F 107) across 61 pairs and 64,422 firm-days from 2014 to 2019, a one standard deviation rise in log PM2.5 moves the premium by 0.73 basis points (95% Anderson-Rubin set −15.5 to +18.1). A pre-registered equivalence test rejects effects larger than 25 basis points, and placebo cities with strong first stages of their own show nothing. Winter-only estimates are positive but rest on the instrument's weakest season. The same instruments fail for Hong Kong, where the reanalysis boundary layer is wrong-signed in winter because the northeast monsoon brings pollution on well-mixed days, on our reading of the seasonal pattern. An exploratory screen of 365 Chinese cities finds such inversions in 22, almost all south of 28°N, so dispersion instruments need a seasonal sign check.

detail.abstract: This study presents a new framework to evaluate administrative plans and explore improvement proposals from a long-term perspective that incorporates the methodology of "Imaginary Future Generations" (IFGs), which has been proven to be effective for generating futurability of individuals. The effectiveness of this framework was verified through a discussion experiment involving local government officials from Yahaba Town in Iwate Prefecture, Japan. Specifically, using the town's urban planning masterplan as a base for discussion, officials worked in groups representing current generations and IFGs. The groups first evaluated the masterplan and suggested improvements from their separate perspectives, and then built a consensus based on the group's proposals to create a final unified set of proposals. From the discussion contents and evaluation results of each group, we found that, compared to the current generation groups, the IFG groups had a stronger tendency to focus on addressing challenges requiring a long-term approach, as well as the coexistence of urban and rural areas. Other differences observed between these groups included perception of the town's challenges, risk awareness of future issues, and plan evaluation results. Consensus-building between groups enabled the two perspectives to be consolidated in evaluation and policy proposals. Results of questionnaire given to the participants indicated that evaluators in the IFG groups exhibited more significant changes in perception through the evaluation process, suggesting a tendency toward increased empathy for future generations. The findings of this study should contribute to developing a new methodology for evaluating administrative plans from the perspectives of sustainability and futurability.

detail.abstract: Valuable materials are frequently discarded because potential reuse opportunities remain invisible or disconnected from those who need them. This Viewpoint introduces the Social Resource Network (SRN), a socio-technical framework for circular waste matchmaking that connects waste generators with potential reusers across households, businesses, communities, and ecological systems. Its central mechanism, bidirectional resource stream mapping (BRSM), pairs participants’ waste profiles with resource-need profiles to identify exchanges according to material type, proximity, quality, quantity, and timing. A six-step process, list, classify, match, confirm, exchange, and verify, structures these interactions, with compliance checks for restricted material streams. Recurring resource flows offer opportunities for forecasting and sustained local exchange networks. The framework emphasizes inclusive participation through mobile applications, SMS, community ambassadors, and institutional interfaces, with artificial intelligence serving as an optional supporting tool. SRN proposes prioritizing resource connections before disposal or processing, complementing existing recycling systems and extending circular participation beyond established industrial clusters. The article presents a conceptual framework rather than an empirically validated implementation.

detail.abstract: Educational policy implementation consistently encounters similar challenges across diverse contexts, indicating systematic implementation challenges rather than random failures. This paper introduces the Education Trilemma framework to explain persistent Outcome-Based Education (OBE) implementation challenges. Drawing on the Mundell-Fleming impossible trinity, we argue that educational systems face inherent tensions between three fundamental objectives: learning outcomes quality, teaching effectiveness, and stakeholder satisfaction. Like monetary policy trilemmas, institutions can optimize at most two objectives simultaneously, creating systematic trade-offs that explain implementation variability. This framework provides theoretical insights into educational policy implementation while offering practical guidance for policymakers who must acknowledge these structural constraints rather than assume stakeholder alignment.

detail.abstract: AI governance programs begin with policies, principles, committees, and reviews. These manual controls decide whether a system may be built and deployed. They do not show that the system running today is the system that was approved, and a program that rests on them alone tends toward paper compliance: complete documents and unproven operation. This paper proposes a framework of 36 automatic controls that the AI delivery and runtime pipeline enforces or evidences by machine, for predictive, generative, and agentic systems. The controls fall into five phases: fixing the approved baseline and its authority, versioning everything that shapes behavior, proving the release candidate, capturing what actually ran, and stopping, restoring, and retiring. For each control the paper states the artifact it protects, the evidence a machine produces, an audit test, and the limit of that evidence. The framework draws on recent work on governance as code, pipeline-embedded evidence, and runtime enforcement, and on established configuration-management practice. We argue that the extent, timing, and depth of every control should follow the calculated exposure to loss of each AI system in scope and the cost of enforcement, above the minimums the law sets. The result gives chief AI officers and AI architects a checklist for gap analysis, a five-level scale for maturity assessment, and criteria for comparing AI GRC platforms. The controls were derived through a structured synthesis of AI-governance literature, security and configuration-management standards, production-ML guidance, and agentic-AI threat guidance, and were practically validated through negative audit tests, traceability tests, and expert review; the framework has not yet been validated through multi-organization empirical field research.

detail.abstract: Two-stage chance-constrained programs with finite, equiprobable scenario support are NPhard due to combinatorial violation-set selection. Exact Benders decomposition (BD) methods struggle with large-scale instances lacking relatively complete recourse, where enforcing feasibility while searching over violation sets creates a computational bottleneck. We develop a learning-guided approach that trains a deep-learning scenario ranker to predict the violation set and identify scenarios to enforce in reduced linear programs solved using BD. Prediction errors are corrected through iterative repair and swap operations. Repairs add excluded but infeasible scenarios to the enforced subset; swaps use feasibility-cut counts to exchange difficult enforced scenarios with low-ranked scenarios in the predicted violation set. An optional local search improves the objective when the chance constraint is binding. We evaluate the approach on a Texas-inspired capacity expansion model with loss-of-load probability constraints, a demanding instance of this problem class. Trained on single-zone, 100-scenario instances, the ranker identifies an initial neighborhood containing the entire optimal violation set in 94.6% of runs across one-to three-zone networks with 100-300 scenarios. Across nine configurations, repair and swap operations increase the average share of optimal violators recovered from 82.0% to 91.6%. The approach achieves a mean optimality gap of 0.66%, with computation times 63.7-79.5% below exact decomposition. For larger networks, the approach recovers three of five known six-zone optima and produces feasible solutions for networks of up to ten zones. The chance constraint is binding in nearly 99% of these instances, suggesting that the resulting decisions are not overly conservative.

The case illustrates how an organised capacity to formulate proposals can coexist with limited authority over implementation.

detail.abstract: The generalized nested logit model extends the nested logit model by allowing each product to belong to multiple nests. The overlapping nests in the generalized nested logit model can capture complex substitution patterns, and the model has found applications in many areas. We study the assortment optimization problem under the generalized nested logit model and prove that it is NP-hard when there are only two nests or when any two distinct nests have at most one product in common. Motivated by these complexity results, we introduce novel concepts of product and nest graphs that capture which products are included in which nests. We use the tree decompositions of the graphs to characterize when the assortment optimization problem admits efficient solution methods. When the treewidth of a product graph is bounded, the assortment optimization problem can be solved in polynomial time. If the treewidth of the product graph is unbounded but the treewidth of the nest graph is bounded, then there exists a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme. These results represent the first polynomial-time algorithms for assortment optimization under the generalized nested logit model. Our numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that the generalized nested logit model provides a better fit to the data than many existing models in the literature.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how good governance can improve transparency and accountability in the financial management of the Bandung City Government through a literature review. It synthesizes ten studies addressing local government financial management, good governance, financial reporting quality, government information systems, internal auditing, and public data disclosure. The reviewed literature indicates that the Bandung City Government has made efforts to apply the principles of transparency, accountability, effectiveness, and efficiency in managing its Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD). Nevertheless, the studies also identify gaps between budget planning and realization, less-than-optimal expenditure realization, and the need to strengthen oversight and coordination among local government agencies. Other studies associate financial reporting quality with good governance, employee competence, accounting information systems, the Regional Government Information System (SIPD), and internal auditing. Public information initiatives, including Satu Data Kota Bandung and Open Data Kota Bandung, provide channels through which government data can be made available to the public. Overall, the synthesis suggests that good governance should not be assessed solely in terms of administrative compliance. It also requires accessible and usable public information, substantive accountability, reliable information systems, competent human resources, and effective oversight. Since this paper synthesizes previously published studies and does not collect new primary data, its conclusions are limited by the scope and quality of the selected literature.

detail.abstract: India has announced a $9.1 billion semiconductor incentive package through the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), aiming to establish domestic chip fabrication capabilities and capture a share of the global $600+ billion semiconductor market. This paper provides a quantitative assessment of India's semiconductor strategy in the context of global fab economics, infrastructure requirements, and the competitive landscape shaped by the US CHIPS Act ($52.7B), the European Chips Act ($43B), and similar initiatives in Japan, China, South Korea, and Southeast Asia. We construct a comparative framework for fab cost analysis across process nodes, model the infrastructure constraints (water, power, talent) that determine fab viability, and evaluate India's incentive competitiveness against peer nations. Our analysis nds that India's scal incentives cover approximately 17% of the US CHIPS Act quantum, with a per-fab incentive density that is competitive for mature-node (28nm90nm) fabs but insucient for leadingedge (sub-7nm) fabrication. The Tata-PSMC Dholera fab, at $11 billion for 50,000 wafers per month, represents India's rst large-scale foray and is projected to reach commercial production by 20282029, placing it within a narrowing window of opportunity as global foundry capacity expands. We identify critical infrastructure gaps: each advanced fab requires 100200 MW of power and 210 million gallons of water daily, resources that are constrained in the Gujarat and Assam regions where India's fabs are being sited. The talent pipeline, while strengthened by 67,000 engineers trained in the past four years, faces a global shortage of semiconductor PhDs and experienced process engineers. Our ndings suggest that India's semiconductor strategy is viable for mature-node and specialty semiconductor manufacturing but faces signicant headwinds in competing for leading-edge nodes. Policy recommendations include targeted investment in water and power infrastructure for fab clusters, expanded PhD-level semiconductor training programs, and a strategic focus on 28nm and above nodes where India's cost structure is most competitive.

detail.abstract: Purpose-This paper examines whether the widespread use of artificial intelligence (AI) is accompanied by a corresponding diffusion of economic ownership and decision-making authority, or whether the concentration of capital and computing infrastructure may instead produce technological dependency and, ultimately, a loss of decision-making autonomy for firms. Design/methodology/approach-The study is conceptual and analytical. It integrates the theory of barriers to entry (Bain, 1956), transaction cost economics (Williamson, 1985), the switching-cost literature and corporate finance theory to analyse the AI value chain layer by layer. Secondary evidence is drawn from the OECD, the International Energy Agency, the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC), the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) and the Stanford AI Index. Findings-The paper identifies a structural paradox in the AI economy: access to AI tools is becoming cheaper, while the infrastructure layers (chips, energy, data centres and cloud computing) are capital-intensive and concentrated. Its central contribution is a mechanism through which dependence on shared infrastructure and shared models may lead to the homogenisation of economic decisions. This effect is not deterministic; it depends on switching costs, competition among providers, open standards and human oversight. Originality/value-The paper connects the literature on competition in AI infrastructure with the literature on algorithmic monoculture, proposes five testable hypotheses with a measurement design, and argues that technological dependency risk should be treated as a distinct dimension of feasibility assessment for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

detail.abstract: Financial institutions use historical simulation to estimate value-at-risk (VaR) and expected shortfall (ES), but incomplete price histories, especially for illiquid assets, leave uncertainty about portfolio losses. A historical-parametric framework addresses this problem by assigning distributions to missing market factors, constructing a profit-and-loss distribution for each historical day, and mixing these distributions before extracting risk. We extend this framework beyond independent shocks and perfectly correlated groups by modeling partial dependence. A low-rank-plus-diagonal representation preserves supplied factor marginals and supports local Edgeworth evaluation with characteristic-function fallback. The construction accommodates Gaussian factors and general normal variance-mean mixtures. Ten paired simulated Treasury histories compare the resulting Partial method with Independent and Grouped against a finite-history reference evaluated by stratified Monte Carlo. Across the common Gaussian and normal-inverse-Gaussian scenarios, Partial's mean absolute relative VaR and ES errors remain below 0.46%. A 5% mean joint-error criterion identifies where simpler methods provide adequate accuracy. In the tested normal-inverse-Gaussian setting, Independent requires weaker dependence and Grouped stronger dependence than under Gaussian factors. These setting-specific applicability regions identify when retaining intermediate dependence materially improves tail-risk measurement.

detail.abstract: Value at Risk (VaR) is widely used to measure downside market risk, but VaR models can differ in both performance and reliability across market conditions. This study compares Historical Simulation, GARCH(1,1)-t, and GJR-GARCH(1,1)-t for estimating the 99% VaR of the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY). Overall performance is evaluated using coverage, accuracy, and clustering metrics, while reliability is assessed by examining performance consistency across volatility regimes, market direction, and stress periods. GJR-GARCH(1,1)-t provides the best overall balance across evaluation measures and maintains comparatively strong performance across market conditions, while Historical Simulation shows greater sensitivity to regime changes and consistently slower adjustment during stress periods. The results suggest that VaR models should be evaluated not only by their overall performance but also by how consistently they perform across changing market conditions and whether their relative advantages persist.

detail.abstract: Stochastic asset-liability models (ALM) for defined benefit pension funds are usually calibrated to historical, stationary distributions, so the low-carbon transition is absent from the funding-ratio tail that trustees monitor. This paper builds a simple climate-integrated stochastic ALM (CI-SALM) for a stylised, fully funded fund invested 60% in equities and 40% in bonds. Transition variables from the NGFS Phase V Below 2°C and Delayed Transition scenarios size a one-off transition shock to equities, fossil-fuel holdings and corporate credit when markets recognise the policy, and move the long-run real interest rate. A small natural-capital productivity drag lowers dividends, wage-linked liability growth and the real rate together. Physical risk is excluded. Across 20 independent runs of 10,000 paths each over 2025 to 2055, compared with a traditional model on the same random numbers, the 5th-percentile funding ratio in 2055 is 4.5 percentage points lower in the disorderly scenario and 1.6 points lower in the orderly scenario, and the probability of ending below 80% funded rises from 11.9% to 14.4%. The gap stays positive in every sensitivity test on the benchmark fund and increases to 9.9 percentage points under severe stress, but its size depends on judgement-based assumptions, which are disclosed and tested.

detail.abstract: We study dynamic multidimensional screening by a seller with fixed capacity. Consumers privately differ in their valuations and in whether they value future purchases. Future discounts can compensate loyal consumers for costly access requirements, or ordeals, but cannot relax current payment constraints. With constant ordeal costs within each group, prices alone are optimal without payment constraints. When payment capacity equals valuation, ordeals are necessary if loyal consumers find them less costly and can be confined to these consumers. Ordeals can remain optimal when loyals find them more costly and may also be imposed on one-time buyers. In this benchmark, surplus maximization requires ordeals, even when prices alone maximize profit.

detail.abstract:
Emerging technologies are reshaping economic competitiveness, public governance, and national security, yet their benefits remain unevenly distributed across regions. This report examines how Latin American and Caribbean countries adopt and develop artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, fifth generation mobile networks, quantum computing, and cybersecurity capabilities. It assesses the structural conditions underlying regional technological dependence and identifies policy priorities for strengthening innovation, resilience, and participation in the global digital economy.

The study combines quantitative evidence from fourteen established indices, reports, and secondary sources with qualitative analysis of grey literature and selected case studies. Its comparative approach situates regional developments alongside technological advances in North America, Europe, and Asia. The analysis considers investment, infrastructure, human capital, institutional capacity, regulatory frameworks, and international cooperation to explain differences in technological readiness and development.

Findings indicate that Latin America and the Caribbean remain predominantly consumers of imported technologies, with limited capacity to generate and commercialize domestic innovations. Insufficient research funding, fragmented policies, inadequate digital infrastructure, and shortages of specialized professionals constrain progress across the technologies examined. These barriers interact with persistent social inequalities and gaps in rural connectivity, limiting access to technological opportunities and reinforcing disparities within and between countries.

Although several countries demonstrate progress in artificial intelligence, connected industries, telecommunications, and scientific research, regional initiatives remain uneven and insufficiently coordinated. Cybersecurity weaknesses expose critical infrastructure and digital services to growing threats, while limited investment in quantum technologies illustrates the distance separating the region from leading innovation ecosystems. The report argues that technology acquisition alone cannot resolve these challenges: effective integration requires sustained institutional support, locally relevant applications, and governance mechanisms capable of addressing security, ethical, and social implications.

The proposed policy agenda prioritizes increased research and development investment, stronger science and technology education, professional training, expanded broadband connectivity, and secure digital infrastructure. Additional recommendations include establishing innovation hubs, promoting public and private partnerships, harmonizing regional standards, supporting technology transfer, and widening participation in international research and governance networks. Recommendations distinguish responsibilities for regional governments from potential contributions by the United States government and United States Southern Command, including technical assistance, joint research, educational exchanges, and cybersecurity capacity building.

The report concludes that closing the emerging technology gap requires coordinated action linking technological modernization with inclusive development and national security. Long term financing, adaptive regulation, regional collaboration, and stronger relationships among governments, universities, industry, and civil society are essential to reducing dependence and improving competitiveness. Rather than treating emerging technologies as isolated investments, policymakers should integrate them into comprehensive strategies that develop domestic capabilities, protect critical systems, and distribute the benefits of digital transformation more equitably. The framework offers practical priorities for strengthening regional technological autonomy while expanding constructive international cooperation and knowledge exchange.

detail.abstract: Administrative reforms increasingly organize consultation without achieving collaborative governance, yet the two are rarely distinguished claim by claim. This article asks how a temporary parliamentary reform body organizes participation across arenas and transforms contributions into a common administrative record while retaining centralized formal authority, and it reads the result against European consultation standards. We conducted an abductive, interpretive, Gioia-informed document analysis of 44 canonical invitations, minutes, and summaries linked to 23 event identifiers in Albania's Administrative-Territorial Reform 2.0, auditing 40 transformation probes across five complete invitation-minutes-summary chains with a second-coder check. None of the 33 traceable propositions retained speaker attribution in the corresponding summary, 32 of 33 retained geographic context, 13 of 14 applicable conflict markers remained visible (11 of 16 under adjudicated coding), and all five sampled interaction rules were absent from the summaries. Two constructs are grounded: asymmetric responsiveness (the unequal allocation of documented opportunities to obtain a response, contest an interpretation, supplement evidence, or revise the record) and documentary standardization. In form, the process resembles consultation the Council of Europe has judged Charter-compliant, but it falls below the collaborative-governance threshold: the consultation-phase record shows no shared authority, joint action, policy uptake, or durable collaborative capacity.

detail.abstract: Pollution raises climate risk by shifting the distribution of everyday climate shocks, making extreme weather events more frequent and more intense, and by increasing the probability of an irreversible climate collapse. I study the impact of the rst channel on the social cost of carbon, introducing what I call stochastic externalities, in which pollution aects the distribution of random climate damages. Solving the social planner's problem, rst in a three-period model and then extending the analysis to an innite-horizon recursive model, I show that the social cost of carbon gains an additional correction term, equal to the expected marginal damages weighted by the distribution's sensitivity to pollution. This term has closed forms for standard distribution families and nests the standard social cost of carbon. In a DICE-SE model calibrated to 1980-2024 disaster losses, I show that this new channel raises the social cost of carbon by 6.2% in a conservative calibration.

detail.abstract: How much dependence uncertainty can a diversification benefit withstand when every marginal loss law is fixed? We study the smallest weighted 1-Wasserstein perturbation that reverses the Expected Shortfall ranking of two nearby allocations evaluated under a common stressed law. For a positive continuous density on a compact box, exchangeability of the two traded positions eliminates the first-order gain, so the relevant stress radius is rho = s * epsilon^2 for trade size epsilon. At this scale, we establish a Gamma-limit for the rescaled transport energies and prove convergence of the paired risk differences, with the two ES thresholds optimized separately. Coordinatewise quantile restoration incurs a marginal-flux cost, although its leading effects on the two ES values cancel in their difference. The limiting risk profile is continuous and strictly increasing, and its unique zero identifies the asymptotic critical budget. We call the excess over the local-efficiency lower bound the marginal-restoration premium. This premium vanishes exactly when background displacement is cheapest per unit change in portfolio loss. Otherwise it is strictly positive, even when the profile is exactly linear on an initial interval. At equal effective costs, continuous maximum-flow/minimum-cut duality characterizes the right derivative of the critical budget with respect to the background penalty.

detail.abstract: Markets for used vehicles have served as the canonical illustration of adverse selection for more than half a century, yet the degree of informational asymmetry surrounding an individual vehicle has not, to my knowledge, been made an observable and computable quantity. This paper introduces such a quantity, the information sufficiency index, defined as the variance-weighted share of value-relevant uncertainty that available information resolves, and shows that it organizes a wide range of market outcomes. As sufficiency rises, the credible range of value narrows; the probability of trade increases, with a loss-aversion discount that is proportional to residual uncertainty; and market demand shifts upward, raising both the clearing price and the volume of trade. Because information is valuable only if it arrives before a decision is made, the probability of trade is decreasing and convex in response time. Robotaxis, which record their own operation continuously, constitute the limiting case of complete information: the informational friction that impedes the transfer of rights falls to its minimum, and whether such vehicles, which create no driving employment, expand aggregate demand depends on whether an equity index, the share of ownership claims held broadly by households, exceeds an explicit threshold. Every quantity in the framework is computable from a vehicle's identification information and records.

detail.abstract: Aware of the risks that global warming poses to the sustainability of coffee production, companies along the coffee value chain established the Consórcio Cerrado das Águas (CCA), a nonprofit organization aimed at strengthening climate resilience and water security in Brazil's Cerrado Mineiro region. Because watershed resilience depends on decentralized land-use decisions by numerous farmers and municipalities, the CCA operates as a collaborative platform based on polycentric governance, coordinating companies, public authorities, technical partners, and agricultural producers. It mobilizes financial, technical, and in-kind resources to promote regenerative agricultural practices and the restoration and conservation of native vegetation. Member companies provide annual contributions that collectively cover approximately 70% of the CCA's operating costs, while additional funding is secured through public and private grants and institutional partnerships. Municipal governments may also provide in-kind contributions, including labor, seedlings, transportation, and machinery. The CCA further seeks to strengthen farmers' economic incentives through certification schemes, insetting programs, access to green credit, and potential payments for ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration. These resources play a catalytic role by financing coordination, technical assistance, ecosystem restoration, and other transition costs that individual farmers may be unwilling or unable to bear. By reducing financial and institutional barriers to adoption, the CCA facilitates collective action and supports the transition toward more resilient and sustainable land-use practices at the landscape scale.

detail.abstract: We study the effects of pseudo-scientific claims on consumer shopping behavior. Pseudo-scientific claims are product claims that adopt the appearance of scientific evidence (e.g., "clinical study") but lack the rigor of valid scientific methodology. Such claims may mislead consumers if they are perceived as more credible than they actually are. We conduct an incentive-aligned online experiment at a leading beauty retailer to measure how pseudo-scientific claims affect consumer search and purchases. Furthermore, we collect data on consumer beliefs and on the perceived credibility of these claims to investigate the underlying mechanism. We find that pseudo-scientific claims cause consumers to terminate their search earlier and to be more likely to purchase a product carrying such a claim. The effect is driven by consumers misinterpreting numerical information, rather than by costly signaling or credibility transfer from medical research. We discuss implications for regulation.

detail.abstract: The health benefit of retiring a coal plant is usually valued as if retirement removed the plant's historical emissions. For 878 US coal unit exits in 2005–2024, 80% of the fall in sulfur dioxide from its peak had happened by the last full year of operation, mostly before any recorded plan to retire; two thirds of the decade's decline came from units running less. Against a validated counterfactual of matched units, crediting the last full year overstates the benefit 1.7 times over five years and twice over ten; crediting emissions from ten years earlier overstates it four to five times. A pre-registered test at 51 large exits rules out lasting local PM2.5 falls of 1.1 µg/m³, the published closure-month size; sulfate falls by an amount consistent with a reduced-complexity model. Retirement benefits are plausible on average, but most arrived before plants closed.

detail.abstract: Blockchain technology has gained growing scholarly and industrial attention for its ability to improve transparency, optimize operational efficiency, and support food safety protocols in food supply chain (FSC) traceability systems. Yet, despite this fast rise in prominence, current scholarly discourse demonstrates a noticeable gap in knowledge regarding the systemic implementation and wider implications of blockchain in FSC traceability. To fill this research gap, the present study delivers what is, to the best of our knowledge, the first large-scale bibliometric examination exclusively focused on blockchain-enabled FSC traceability. Using 620 publications indexed in the Scopus database, this study maps the intellectual structure of the field and traces the evolution of research themes concerning blockchain-enabled traceability. The review uncovers several dominant thematic trajectories. More specifically, the adoption of blockchain with complementary advanced technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) has become a focal trend. Concurrently, blockchain acts as a mechanism to mitigate concerns related to food safety, authenticity, security, and sustainable supply governance. The findings illustrate the multifaceted utility of blockchain in FSC traceability and signal its potential to impact future trends in supply chain management. Overall, this article addresses a critical gap in the current literature and lays a foundation for further interdisciplinary exploration. By aligning theoretical discourse with practical relevance, the review aims to contribute to the development of transparent, efficient, and sustainable food supply systems, thereby supporting global food safety and security objectives.

detail.abstract: Aim: Population ageing and the growing burden of physical inactivity place substantial pressure on health systems, increasing demand for scalable, safe, and cost-effective interventions. This review appraises the available evidence on structured walking football programmes for middle-aged and older adults, and discusses preliminary implications for cost-effectiveness analysis and healthcare resource allocation. Subject and Methods: A systematic review was conducted on studies evaluating structured walking football programmes, a modified version of football played at walking speed, in middle-aged and older adults were identified, screened, and synthesised narratively, with particular attention to physiological, psychological, and economic outcomes. Results: The included studies reported improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength, mobility, and body composition, together with reductions in blood pressure, fasting glucose, and glycated haemoglobin. These outcomes are directly relevant to the prevention and management of high-cost chronic conditions, including Type 2 Diabetes, hypertension, and selected oncological conditions. Psychological benefits were also described, including better quality of life, greater self-confidence, and fewer depressive symptoms. However, small sample sizes and substantial heterogeneity in study design limit the strength of the evidence. Conclusion: Walking football appears to be a promising, accessible intervention for promoting health in middle-aged and older adults. The current evidence base does not allow firm conclusions on economic implications, nor does it support the direct incorporation of findings into formal economic models and policy frameworks. Nonetheless, preliminary data suggest that per-patient costs may be competitive with those of standard exercise referral schemes, warranting larger and methodologically consistent trials with embedded economic evaluation.

detail.abstract:
Background. Hospitals considering body-worn cameras (BWCs) for serious incidents face distinct questions about what can be lawfully recorded, how disputed events are reviewed, and who can act on the findings.

Objective. To propose a three-gate governance framework for incident-oriented recording in U.S. emergency departments and examine its implications for patient participation, AI-assisted activation, and independent custody.

Approach. This conceptual policy analysis draws on a targeted, non-systematic synthesis of empirical research, selected U.S. legal authorities, and a documentary comparison of two healthcare BWC policies or guidance documents and a federal hospital grievance requirement. An author-involved case and a paired hypothetical illustrate how the proposed pathway would operate.

Analysis. The framework separates evidentiary integrity, accountability activation through independent review, and remedial access. A complaint can enter review whether footage is partial, missing, or lawfully never created. AI may help identify an eligible safety signal, subject to separate human recording authorization. Independent storage may protect originals, while a distinct review function is needed to reach a reasoned disposition and refer matters to an authority able to act.

Conclusion. The proposal yields testable comparisons with existing grievance and BWC practice. Its added value depends on whether it improves the quality and timeliness of decisions without increasing unjustified recording, privacy harms, or barriers to patient participation.

detail.abstract: We examine how patent protection shapes firms’ voluntary disclosure incentives through its effect on financing. We hypothesize that weaker patent protection reduces the collateral value of patents, prompting firms to substitute secured debt with unsecured debt. Because unsecured creditors rely more heavily on information about firms’ future cash flows, this shift increases disclosure incentives. Exploiting the 2014 U.S. Supreme Court Alice decision, which weakened protection for certain patents, we find that more Alice-exposed firms become more forthcoming during earnings conference calls. The disclosure response is stronger among firms facing debt-related financial constraints, firms that previously pledged patents as collateral, and firms with more redeployable patents. However, the response is attenuated among small firms and firms facing greater product market competition, consistent with heightened proprietary costs of disclosure. We also find that affected patents become less likely to be pledged as collateral and that exposed firms reduce their reliance on secured debt. Our findings identify a financing channel through which patent protection influences voluntary disclosure.

detail.abstract: Construction loans change as projects move through different phases from planning through draws, completion, and repayment; however, public bank filings do not record these development stages. This paper examines construction and land-development credit quality using December 2021-2025 FFIEC Call Reports and a 2012-2025 FDIC bank panel. In 2025, domestic-office filings reported $456.1 billion in funded construction and land-development loans, of which $91.1 billion was one-to-four-family residential construction. Reported problem-loan shares differed across residential and other construction categories and moved in opposite directions between 2024 and 2025. In the longer FDIC panel, the conditional association between prior construction concentration and later problem-loan share is positive over 2013-2025 but weaker and statistically inconclusive over 2017-2025. Across eight rolling holdouts (2018-2025), a fitted bank-level model produced higher weighted mean absolute error than a simple prior-bank-share benchmark in every period, while showing lower weighted root mean square error. The paper's contribution is threefold: a reproducible public-data picture of construction-credit heterogeneity, a set of transparent predictive benchmarks against which a stage-informed method should be compared, and a specified project-lifecycle research design that states the hypotheses, evaluation measures, and data requirements needed to test whether development-stage information improves risk measurement. The stage-sensitive test itself requires loan-level histories that are not available in either public dataset.

detail.abstract: Modern macroeconomic theory and global defense strategies operate on the assumption that financial capital and military leverage can secure supply chains during geopolitical crises. This paper challenges that assumption by examining the empirical geological and engineering limits of critical mineral extraction. Focusing specifically on the Bushveld Complex and the Kalahari Manganese Field in South Africa, this doctrine outlines how the concentration of Chromium, Platinum Group Metals, and Manganese creates an insurmountable physical bottleneck. By analyzing deep level mining architecture, defense stockpile deficits, and asymmetric infrastructural threats, this paper establishes that absolute national sovereignty is a physical impossibility. True resilience requires recognizing these resources as an interdependent global network managed by optimized logistical systems rather than isolated national leverage points.

detail.abstract: Shoppers increasingly ask AI assistants whether to buy a product. I audited GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Sonnet 5.5 with 9,168 preregistered prompts each, plus an open-weight model. Most prompts showed one product next to a "Customers also viewed" box of unrelated items. Raising its prices from low to high moved 1-7 purchase ratings by 3 to 9 points on a 0-100 scale but forced yes/no purchase verdicts by 13 to 32 points. The binary effect peaked where the baseline yes-rate was near one half, consistent with a threshold on a small, nearly constant shift in the underlying evaluation. Deriving the decision from the rating with a fixed cutoff did not help, because that cutoff is a threshold too. A stated usual price set the center of an S-shaped drop in deal ratings, and without one the fair price tracked the posted price. When the models advised freely on an HTML product page (Study 3), high rather than low prices next door raised buy recommendations by 11 and 24 points in two of three models. Both the content around a product and the way an assistant turns its evaluation into a decision shape AI shopping advice.

detail.abstract:
This article examines multidimensional human security among older Muslim migrants in Europe through an integrated framework connecting ageing, migration history, religious identity and institutional protection. Drawing on human security theory and intersectionality, the study addresses the limitations of approaches that examine discrimination, socioeconomic vulnerability, healthcare inequalities and institutional representation separately. 

Methodologically, it combines a critical integrative literature review, conceptual analysis and historically contextualised documentary examination. The article proposes five interconnected dimensions of human security: physical security; psychosocial security; health and care security; housing and economic security; and cultural, religious and institutional security. The analysis suggests that insecurity is shaped not by ageing, migration background or religious identity alone, but by interactions between individual circumstances, structural inequalities and access to protective resources. 

Particular attention is devoted to institutional representation, examined through the historical experiences of the Turkish-Islamic Elderly Union (Turks-Islamitische Ouderen Bond, TISBO, founded in 1993) and the Netherlands Islamic Elderly Union (NISBO, founded in 1995) in the Netherlands. These cases illustrate how migrant organisations sought to address housing needs, facilitate access to welfare services and strengthen collective representation, while also highlighting questions of institutional effectiveness and sustainability. The article contributes a population-sensitive conceptual framework in which institutional protection operates both as a distinct security dimension and as a cross-cutting mechanism. It concludes by identifying implications for inclusive ageing policies, equitable service provision, meaningful participation and future comparative research.

detail.abstract: Firms can influence market competition through both their organizational structure and the attention of their managers. We study an oligopoly in which firms choose the number of autonomous divisions and whether their managers account for the effect of their production on aggregate industry output. These choices jointly determine a firm's effective conduct, which measures the extent to which its organization restrains output. We show that every pure-strategy equilibrium has symmetric effective conduct. Our main result is that increasing product substitutability can generate repeated transitions from strategic inattention back to full attention. As products become closer substitutes, a given attentive organization becomes less aggressive, making strategic inattention more attractive. However, establishing an additional division allows firms to compete more aggressively while retaining full attention. We further show that although divisionalization makes an attentive firm more aggressive, its availability can soften market competition by replacing strategic inattention with less aggressive attentive organizations. Relative to the all-inattentive outcome, firms then earn higher profits, while consumer surplus and total welfare decline.

detail.abstract:
This paper reconstructs the intellectual origins of Antitrust 5.0, tracing the evolution of a conceptual framework that connects competition law with technological transformation, economic sovereignty, national security, and geoeconomics.

Drawing on a sequence of fifteen opinion columns published between 2023 and 2026, within an intellectual trajectory beginning in 2017, the paper documents the progressive development of ideas concerning geopolitical rivalry, industrial policy, strategic dependencies, international economic asymmetries, and the changing role of the State in shaping markets.

The analysis examines how developments involving the United States, China, Russia, and the European Union contributed to a growing recognition that competition law cannot be understood independently of the geopolitical structures within which markets operate.

Rather than reformulating the theoretical foundations of Antitrust 5.0, this work documents their intellectual genealogy, identifying the questions, debates, and historical developments that preceded the emergence of the framework.

The paper culminates in the guiding principle of Antitrust 5.0: "Sovereignty outward; contestability inward."  This proposition seeks to reconcile economic sovereignty and national resilience with the preservation of competitive domestic markets.

detail.abstract: Return differences across stocks are not compensation for common risk. We derive an upper bound on the share of these differences that common risk accounts for. The bound holds under every stochastic discount factor and can be estimated using any portfolio. We define common factors as the first ten principal components of stock returns, which explain more return variance than any other ten portfolios. Using a portfolio built from machine-learning forecasts, with out-of-sample Sharpe ratios of 4.02 in U.S. stocks over 1990-2023 and 4.74 in 22 other developed markets over 2000-2023, the bound is 4.7% in the U.S. and 2.4% internationally. With fifty principal components, both bounds rise only to about 10%. These findings challenge the identification of common variation with priced risk: explaining why stocks move together is not the same as explaining why their expected returns differ.

detail.abstract: Growing solar capacity increases grid-constrained curtailment. Developers can mitigate curtailment by expanding grid connections or adding storage. Transmission cost allocation dictates this choice. Yet how this allocation shapes optimal storage duration remains understudied. Our study is among the first to quantify how cost allocation alters storage duration and to measure the resulting welfare loss. We derive a semi-analytical solution for the required storage duration of PV plants and test it against hourly data from 107 PV units in Australia's National Electricity Market. We then calibrate a two-node linear programme to the Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone to find the optimal combination of line capacity and storage duration. The solution predicts surplus energy accurately, with a median observed to-predicted ratio close to 1.0 both in sample and out of sample. In the base case, developers face less than one-sixth of social cost, leading them to build 0.84 MW of line with 4-hour storage per MW of solar, departing from the socially optimal 0.27 MW of line with 7-hour storage. This distortion causes a welfare loss of A$38,984 per MW of solar annually. Oversized lines account for almost the entire loss, while battery duration choice contributes between 0% and 3.1%. Across all sensitivity scenarios in which the trunk network requires expansion, developers consistently prefer maximum line capacity. However, when the trunk network has spare capacity, the annual welfare loss falls to around A$60 per MW of solar. These results suggest that current cost allocation weakens the incentive for developers to substitute storage for line capacity. These findings provide evidence-based insights for policymakers.

detail.abstract: I examine how oil spills from the pipelines that carry crude oil across Nigeria affect agricultural productivity. I combine the geo-referenced register of the national oil spill agency with household surveys and satellite measures of the vegetation of farmland. Guided by a consumer-producer household framework, I estimate an agricultural production function, and I follow farmland before and after its first recorded spill. Relative to farmland far from any spill, farmland near spills loses vegetation: around 5% within two kilometers, falling to about 2% at 15 to 20 kilometers, and the loss grows over the following decade. Much of this difference, however, reflects differences between areas. Relative to farmland of the same local government area, the loss is small for several years and larger a decade later, mainly after the earliest recorded spills. The pattern of the losses along the rivers suggests that part of the damage travels with the water. The loss also appears on land that remains in crops. Household output for the same land and labor is lower near spills, but few surveyed villages are exposed and the estimate is not robust. The results highlight a lasting externality of the oil industry on rural livelihoods, whose assessment depends heavily on the comparison.
